title: Select ordinary rational activities efficiently GIVEN a numeric log-radius bound
statement: Given rational NUMERIC radius B>=1 and promise there exists real theta-star with ||theta-star||2<=B and ||grad F_m(theta-star)||2<=epsilon/32, minimize G=F_m+tau||theta||2^2/2,tau=epsilon/(32B). Convex-gradient monotonicity yields r(r-B)<=B(r+B), hence ||theta_tau||<3B and original gradient<3epsilon/32. Over[-4B,4B]^d, an explicit Poisson-anchor Hessian upper H has log(H+1)=poly_R(L+B). Paid value/moment calls at rational approximations to exp(theta), certified exp rounding and rational convex cutting planes reach objective error<=tau*epsilon^2/[10^5(H+1)^2]. Strong convexity gives original mean error<epsilon/4, and ordinary positive rational exp rounding adds<epsilon/4. Work/RAM/output bits are poly_R(L+B), with B charged NUMERICALLY, not only bits(B). Thus an explicit computable polynomial-in-L radius theorem suffices to finish global selection, without an interior-margin/covariance-floor promise. This does NOT provide that missing global radius.
